newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil January trade balance due Wednesday.
newsitem.headline: Brazil January trade balance due Wednesday.

text.p: Brazil's trade balance for January is expected to be announced at 1100 local time/0800 EST/1300 GMT Wednesday, finance and industry and commerce ministry spokespeople said.
Foreign trade secretary Mauricio Cortes told Reuters Friday the January figure would be in equilibrium.
He denied reports that the surprise result after seven continuous months of deficits was because of problems with the new SISCOMEX import registration system.
Cortes said importers had increased their purchases in December because of anticipated problems, "even fear" of the SISCOMEX system, which came on line January 1.
"SISCOMEX itself had no effect (on the balance)," he said.
According to internal government documents, Brazil posted a $200 million-plus surplus up to January 28, with exports of $3.13 billion and imports of $2.91 billion.
Average daily imports in the first week of the month were a low $3.3 million, picking up gradually to average $153.1 million by January 28.
It was not until January 15 that imports exceeded $200 million in a single day. In the second week of the month, the highest daily import figure was $91.9 million.
Average daily exports by January 28 were $164.8 million.
A January surplus or equilibrium would be the first positive monthly result since last May. Brazil posted a record trade gap of $5.54 billion in 1996.
